name: Samaritans (UK & Ireland)
summary: 24/7 emotional support line for anyone in distress or experiencing suicidal thoughts.

sections.title: About Samaritans
sections.text: Samaritans is a registered charity aimed at providing emotional support to anyone in emotional distress, struggling to cope, or at risk of suicide throughout the United Kingdom and Republic of Ireland. Founded in 1953 by Reverend Chad Varah in London, Samaritans pioneered the concept of crisis helplines. The organization operates with a simple vision: fewer people die by suicide. Samaritans believes that having someone to talk to, without judgment, can be life-changing and potentially life-saving.

sections.title: Who Should Contact Samaritans
sections.text: You can contact Samaritans about anything that's troubling you, no matter how large or small the issue feels. You don't have to be suicidal to reach out—Samaritans is there for anyone struggling to cope, feeling overwhelmed, worried about someone else, or just needing someone to talk to. Common reasons people contact Samaritans include relationship problems, loss and bereavement, financial worries, mental health concerns, loneliness, and thoughts of suicide. Whatever you're going through, Samaritans volunteers will listen without judgment.

sections.title: How to Contact Samaritans
sections.text: Call 116 123 free from any phone, 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. This number is free to call from landlines and mobiles in the UK and Ireland. You can also email jo@samaritans.org and receive a response within 24 hours. In-person visits are available at local Samaritans branches—visit samaritans.org to find your nearest branch and opening hours. Welsh speakers can call the Welsh Language Line on 0808 164 0123 (7pm-11pm daily). Samaritans also offers a self-help app with guided exercises for emotional support.

sections.title: What Happens When You Contact Samaritans
sections.text: When you contact Samaritans, you'll speak with a trained volunteer who will give you the time and space to talk about what's on your mind. Volunteers practice active listening—they won't judge you, give advice, or tell you what to do. Instead, they help you explore your feelings and thoughts at your own pace. Calls are confidential and won't appear on your phone bill in a way that identifies Samaritans. You can remain anonymous if you wish. There's no time limit on calls, and you can contact Samaritans as often as you need.

sections.title: Additional Samaritans Services
sections.text: Beyond the helpline, Samaritans runs programs to support mental health across communities. The Listener Training helps volunteers develop skills for providing emotional support. Samaritans partners with Network Rail, schools, prisons, and workplaces to train staff in suicide prevention. The Step by Step service supports schools after a suspected suicide. Samaritans also works to reduce harmful media portrayal of suicide and advocated for the Suicide Prevention Act. The organization trains thousands of new volunteers each year to ensure support is always available.
